utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Cicak, we will continue with the documentary exhibits. Exhibit 12, please. As I forecast yesterday, a document that won't take up much time, but a document of reference. From yesterday, if you could separate the one from the other, please, Mr. Usher. Lay the English version on the ELMO. This is a document, Mr. Cicak, dated the 23rd of August, being a proposal for the regionalisation of the municipal committees of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina, said to be pursuant to conclusions of the main committee on the 6th of August, the goal said to be to establish closest possible links amongst the committees on a territorial basis and thereby to promote the preconditions for the political and territorial linking of the Croatian people for which special programmes will have to be designed. That's how it sets out at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Under the regional committees, number 1 is the Travnik region, with nine municipalities listed, and we can see those for ourselves.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This document is signed by Kostroman only. Did you know anything about the establishment of these regional committees?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Regarding the establishment of regional committees in Central Bosnia and the region of Herzegovina, I was aware of that, but not about the other details. This was written by Mr. Kostroman probably on the basis of a decision by the main board, though it is not stated that that is an abstract from that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. The next exhibit is Exhibit 14, a document from the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina, municipal organisation of Busovaca, dated the 29th of August, said to be a decision on the functioning of the municipal organisation. At the foot of the first English page and Article 2 in the original, please, "The decision to change the functioning of the municipal HDZ B and H organisation in Busovaca to exceptional or wartime conditions shall be made by the executive board of the municipal HDZ BH board in Busovaca at its special session." Then Article 3: "After the decision is made to change the functioning to exceptional or wartime conditions, the executive board of the municipal HDZ B and H board shall become the command of the municipal HDZ BH organisation in Busovaca in exceptional or wartime conditions. The president of the municipal HDZ B and H organisation in Busovaca shall become the commander, and his assistants, the deputy presidents, secretaries, and treasurer shall have the same post in the command. Presidents of the HDZ BH branches shall become branch commanders. The HDZ B and H command in Busovaca shall work jointly in exception or wartime conditions on the basis of actual or free estimate of the exceptional or wartime conditions, all with the goal of protecting the lives and property of Croatian citizens." Were you aware of the making of this order or of the making of this decision?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were you a party to the making of this decision?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In whom did this decision vest power; which individuals?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: The greatest power was given to the president of the municipal board of the HDZ of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you agree to that happening at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Could I agree or not is not relevant, because the situation was such that it was impossible to change anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And, of course, the president at the time was who?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: The president at the time was Mr. Dario Kordic, and he was vested with the greatest powers in exceptional and wartime conditions that set in the territory of Busovaca municipality or, rather, in the territory of the regional community and Bosnia and Herzegovina as a whole or, rather, each president was vested with such powers, if there were such decisions in other municipal boards of the HDZ in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Looking at Article 13, please, reading as follows: "All the sessions of the command of the municipal HDZ B and H organisation in Busovaca and the sessions of the Security Council of HDZ B and H in Busovaca shall be held in secret and without the presence of public. All written documentation of the command of the municipal organisation and the Security Council of the HDZ B and H in Busovaca shall be strictly controlled, strictly confidential, and not available to the public." Article 14, "The release of information to the press shall be made only by the command of the municipal HDZ B and H organisation in Busovaca." So there was that restriction on publicity on any occasion when these articles were effective; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And who was to determine when these powers came into operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Who was able to determine when these exceptional circumstances were such that these provisions were effective? Which person or body determined --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: The body was the municipal board of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If we look at the last page of the document, we see that this one is signed, or there's a place for a signature. No signature itself, but the name is Dario Kordic. Yes? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not getting any translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. I said at the end of the document, is there a place -- can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: At the end of the document there is a place for the signature of Dario Kordic, but in fact, no actual signature?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: There's no signature. A sentence has been added, that the decision was adopted at a meeting of the municipal board of the HDZ in Busovaca on the 29th of August, 1991. I'm not sure that Mr. Kordic did not sign this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next exhibit is Exhibit 16, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No, I'm finished the questions in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not sure -- maybe the witness is wanting to say something. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Is there something you want to say, Mr. Cicak, or are you waiting for another question from me?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I just wanted to say that no one, and especially Mr. Dario Kordic, abided by this decision, because it is stated here that all decisions regarding a state of war or exceptional circumstances should be taken by the municipal board. The municipal board never met to take any such decision. All decisions were taken by Mr. Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Exhibit 16, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: From the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Security Council, marked "Strictly Confidential" and dated the 18th of September of 1991, being the conclusions of the Security Council at its session on that date, and in paragraph 1 of the conclusions, it says that "The Security Council will from now on be called the crisis staff," with the following members, and it identifies Kljuic, Boban, others, including Kostroman, Bozidar Skravan, Bozo Rajic, and Bruno Stojic. It sets out, three paragraphs thereafter, that the president of the crisis staff is Kljuic and the vice-president is Boban. And then, at paragraph 5, please, it says: "Stjepan Kljuic is required immediately to contact the leadership of the SDA/Party of Democratic Action/ and to seek a political declaration from them, but the crisis staff shall develop plans of action both with and without the SDA, and shall undertake concrete measures for this purpose." At paragraph 8, there was the recommendation to the municipalities that they should not send recruits to the army, and that no mobilisation be permitted except for mobilisation carried out through the HDZ crisis staffs. We can see that this order or decision comes over the signature of -- signatures of Kostroman and Kljuic. Were you aware of these decisions or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Nice, but going on to your question about this decision, I should like to learn from the witness, through you, if there is a relationship between the previous document and the document we are reviewing now, because in the previous document the head of the Security Council -- it is the document Z14, and the one we're looking at now is Z16. In Z14, on which you have asked questions, mention is made of the formation of a Security Council in Busovaca, and then we see the same Security Council in the next document with, at the head, the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is it the same Security Council that is being referred to in both documents? That is my question, so that the Chamber is able to follow more closely the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You've heard the question of Judge Bennouna, Mr. Cicak, but is the position this, that document Z14 is the HDZ for the municipal organisation in Busovaca, whereas 16 is the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina itself? Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and would you be so kind as to give me the date when the document in Busovaca was adopted?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That was on the 29th of August, 1991.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that Your Honours now have insight into the fact that we preceded the presidency of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that the document adopted in Busovaca preceded the document that was adopted in Sarajevo. So the document in Sarajevo came later, and it has no connection with the document adopted in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: But of course the crisis staff composition for the party as a whole, as formulated in Sarajevo, is different, of course, from the formulation of the crisis staff in the locality of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Indeed. It is only normal that it should differ, because this is a crisis staff or, rather, the transfer of the presidency of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina into a crisis staff covering the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina, whereas in Busovaca we are talking about the municipal organisation of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina for Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I hope that clarifies the matter for Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you. The decision of the 29th of August, 1991, in Busovaca, did it prepare the decision taken at the level of the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Did it prepare the decision of the 18th of September, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You've heard the Judge's question, Mr. Cicak; are you able to help with an answer to that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Absolutely not. That was not in preparation for this decision at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The decision in Busovaca was taken prior to the other decision, and the two are not connected.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May we move now then, please, to Exhibit 18. Again, this is a document from the party of Bosnia-Herzegovina as a whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If these are core bundle documents, Mr. Nice, if you would --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- let us know that, as you did yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I did yesterday. Could I give you the numbers of the ones I've dealt with?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm so sorry to have overlooked that. While they're being distributed, the numbers of the first one, Z12, were pages 5803 -- I'm only giving you the first page number, of course -- and the number of Z14 was 5799. The number of 16 was 5786, and the number of this document, Z18, is 5782.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This document, then, dated the 8th of October and coming from the presidency of the party as a whole, or its crisis staff, said to be conclusions of a joint meeting held on the 8th of October, has at paragraph 3 of the conclusions that "The Croatian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina is called upon to reject all calls for mobilisation, recruitment, and financing of the army." And at paragraph 4, this: "The Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina shall continue to advocate an independent and indivisible Bosnia and Herzegovina if that is possible, but in the event of the break-up of Bosnia and Herzegovina our recommendation to the leaders of the Muslim people is after the secession of the so-called Serbian territories in Bosnia and Herzegovina that the Muslims remain together with the Croats territorially, and that we link our territories with the Republics of Croatia and Slovenia confederally or by treaty."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Cicak, first of all, were you ever aware of the decision that's set out here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of this decision. I learnt about it somewhat later because I was personally informed about it by the president of the Croatian Democratic Union, Mr. Stjepan Kljuic. Next question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And what do you say as to the proposed linking of the territories with Croatia and Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Allow me first to answer the question regarding point 3. This was the general position of the Croatian people not to respond to calls for mobilisation, recruitment, and financing of the BH army or, rather, the JNA army, because the JNA had already conducted an attack against the Republic of Croatia and Slovenia. So it was only normal to reject any connections with the JNA army because Bosnia-Herzegovina -- or, rather, the Croatian people believed that was essential. As for point 4, it typically reflects the position of the presidency of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that is to continue to advocate an indivisible Bosnia-Herzegovina with all peoples living in it on an equal footing, but in the event of a break-up, which was already a manifest tendency, the Bosniak people is called upon here -- though they are called the Muslims in this text -- to stay together with the Croats in one entity and then to try to establish confederal or contractual relations with the Republic of Croatia. I do not understand -- I don't think anyone can understand -- why the Republic of Slovenia is mentioned here, because it has no geographic, ethnic, or any other connections. Whether this was an error or whether it really was considered at the time, I don't know, but when I was reading through this document, I understood what it aspired for, but what was essential for me was that the presidency sought to preserve Bosnia-Herzegovina as an indivisible entity, and the call for unity with the Republic of Croatia was simply in the interest of defence against threats coming against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next exhibit is Z20 -- no, I'm so sorry; Z19. Core bundle page 5776.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You may or may not be able to help us with this. It's a single sheet, as presented, with the English translation on the reverse of the photocopy of the hand-written original. Looking at the hand-written original, have you ever seen this document before, other than seeing it here at court?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is a document I have not seen before, and I cannot say what it relates to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Insofar as there may be reference to monies coming to Busovaca, were you aware of whether monies came to the party in Busovaca, and if so, how?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were two ways that monies arrived in Busovaca. The first was direct financing of the needs of the HDZ from the Republic of Croatia, that is, directly from Zagreb. Another way of money coming in was from the sale of weapons, which was coming to Bosnia-Herzegovina free of charge and was being sold at a high price to HDZ members who could afford to buy them. Of course, what happened was that poor people would sell a part of their own property. I don't know how the interpreters are going to translate this. They would sell livestock to be able to procure automatic weapons. So my assumption, and it is just an assumption, so please don't take note of it, that this was simply a bill being shown to Mr. Kordic for monies received, but please don't take this officially.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The money coming from Zagreb, who brought it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: The main link between the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the part that split from Mr. Kljuic, was linked to Mr. Mate Boban, and Mr. Mate Boban was the main link between Zagreb and this part of Bosnia, the so-called Travnik region and the whole of Herzegovina or, rather, all the HDZ organisations in Herzegovina who were linked to Mr. Mate Boban. He was the undisputed chief in all these things, especially when it came to finance.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did money come in cash or in some other form?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Would you speak a little more loudly, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did it come in cash or in some other form?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I wasn't implying you but the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: The money came in two forms, in cash and in weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: When it came in cash, did you see it arrive or did you just learn of its coming?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't learn about it, but I saw it in person, because on one occasion I had the opportunity to be in Mr. Boban's company when he gave a certain sum of money for the basic organisation in Vares or, rather, the municipal HDZ organisation in Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you remember what quantity of money was involved on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Money was never counted, and the amount of money was never important for Mr. Boban.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you very much. Let's move on to the next exhibit, 20, please, core document page 5774, this being a document of the party at the Croatian Regional Community of Travnik level, as described, dated the 4th of November, the subject being simply the meeting, your name being listed beside "Busovaca," along with others, including Dario Kordic. In the conclusions, at paragraph 1, it's stated that Stjepan Kljuic was not present, although he had been duly and timely invited to the meeting. At paragraph 2, conclusion number, and then it reads "02-POV - 1/91," "OD 20" -- of the 22nd of October, 1991, "sent to Dr. Franjo Tudjman, was unanimously supported. Members of the Croatian Regional Community of Travnik promise to respect the secrecy of this information." You were listed as being present at this meeting. Were you present?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you help at all with the confidential and secret communication sent to Zagreb, to Tudjman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know why this was called secret, but at the time we probably thought this was necessary because of the police and other military intelligence organisations that probably existed in Bosnia-Herzegovina. So this letter was a secret one, although it could have been public. It said the following: That young men would voluntarily take part in the defence of the Republic of Croatia and that they would volunteer to go to the Republic of Croatia to defend it from the aggressor. On the other hand, it said that the Croatian community or, rather, the Democratic Croatian Community of Bosnia-Herzegovina, would make every effort to give humanitarian and military assistance to the Republic of Croatia. At that time, there were drives to collect clothes and everything else that is needed when a country is attacked and when another country should help it. At the time in Bosnia and Herzegovina, there was not a war there, but it was obvious that it would start soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next exhibit, please, Exhibit 21, 1, but it is in the core bundle at page 5767. Mr. Cicak, the original is not very easy to read, but I'll read it in the English, and if you can follow it, I would be grateful. Is this a document, dated the 5th of November of 1991, headed "The Travnik Regional Committee of the Party," relating to a written response to Mr. Kljuic's inappropriate ultimatum to Mr. Kordic? And just before we read the body of the letter, in the postscript at the end, it being set out that he was sending, that is, Mr. Kordic was sending a copy of this fax, addressed to Mr. Kljuic, to all representatives of the Travnik Regional Community of the party. Did you receive a copy of this letter?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: The letter was discussed within the municipal committee in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. It reads, "Following our telephone conversation on the 5th of November around 11.30 hours when I was put through to you by General-Secretary Ivan Markesic and when you told me in a 30-second speech, and I quote, 'Kordic, if you do not appear in my office tomorrow at 8 o'clock, you will be brought in by the police,' I'm sending you the following response. "By the time you received this fax, you will probably be familiar with the written conclusions reached at the meeting of the Travnik Regional Community held in Busovaca on 4th November, fully supporting all the clear and unambiguous positions of the Travnik Regional Community. "As we no longer live in a time of uniformity of view and blind obedience, I feel compelled to remind you that your position as president in the Bosnia HDZ implicitly carries the obligation of living and acting among the party membership and respecting the wish of the responsible representatives of the Croats of this area, that you finally attend at least one meeting of the Travnik Regional Community. I wish to inform you that the most responsible Croatian representatives of the municipalities of the Travnik Regional Community have not given me the authority to speak with you personally and particularly not tête-à-tête about the fate of our people, but if you insist, with inappropriate threats and ultimatums on a meeting, it may take place, but only with all the leaders of the Travnik Regional Community in Busovaca." Did you know in advance, Mr. Cicak, that that letter was going to be sent?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I knew that the letter would be sent because we had discussed it at the municipal committee meeting of the HDZ of Busovaca. The point was that the president of the HDZ of BH, Stjepan Kljuic, was busy at the state presidency, and it was very difficult for him to attend all meetings at regional communities and at local levels. That is one thing. Another thing is that the Croatian Regional Community of Travnik, in relation to the BH HDZ, was getting stronger and stronger, and that was the objective of this document. It is quite inconceivable that a member of a municipal committee, who was at a far lower level of the president of the HDZ, addresses the president of the party in this way. I mean this is not customary in the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And, of course, and I take you back to the document, the last document we looked at, which reflected a meeting at which you attended, had Dario Kordic signing as president of the Croatian Regional Community of Travnik. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean this document that we've just been discussing?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The previous document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: The letter? Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Forget this question, Mr. Cicak, because I can deal with it with the next exhibit. Thank you. Exhibit 22, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I see the signature of Dario Kordic here on this letter. I don't know what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Core document page 5765, could the Tribunal, please, and my friends opposite, note that on the English version, the first half dozen lines, which begin "Annex 16" and goes down to what looks like a horizontal line, can be deleted. They aren't part of the original document. They are some other annotation. So the document starts from "Herzegovina Regional Community, Travnik Regional Community," and it's the conclusions of the joint meeting of the Herzegovina Regional Community and the Travnik Regional Community. And before we come to the conclusions, Mr. Cicak, would you please turn to the end of the document and to where you can find the signatures?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And are these documents signed by Boban, on behalf of Herzegovina, and Dario Kordic, as president of the Travnik Regional Community?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I haven't got the signature here. This document was not signed by Mate Boban. And the signature of Mr. Dario Kordic is among the signatures of the participants in this meeting, but not as a signatory of the document, which is quite customary, because I do not see any reason why he would sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I can see there's a problem about the subscript of this document, and I'll deal with that. It may be that there's a better version of the original from which the translation was taken. But for the time being, the subscript and signatures on the English version must be queried until I can replace it with a better original.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The conclusions read as follows: Number 1, picking it up about three lines in, "... continue to support the unanimously-approved declarations and conclusions adopted in the agreements with President Franjo Tudjman on the 13th and 20th of June of 1991 in Zagreb." At the end of that paragraph is there set out that, "the communities jointly and unanimously adopt the decision that the Croatian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina must finally institute a decisive and active policy in order to bring about our age-old dream - a common Croatian state." And the next paragraph goes on to say, "In order for this historical goal to become our reality in the near future, the two regional communities call for the formulation and declaration of legal and political documents (the proclamation of a Croatian banovina or entity in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the organisation of a referendum to join the Republic of Croatia...) as the initial phase leading towards the final solution of the Croatian question and the creation of a sovereign Croatia within its ethnic and historical (currently possible) borders." Can you help us in two ways, please, Mr. Cicak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: First, as to the alleged agreements of the 13th and 20th of June, 1991, made with Dr. Franjo Tudjman in Zagreb, can you help us with what they were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot tell you anything about these agreements because I was not in the presence of Mr. Franjo Tudjman, and that was a group of Bosnian Croats that was present there at Mr. Franjo Tudjman's. Later on, I found out about the details that were being discussed, but it is precisely this part that was discussed, the one that relates to this text from paragraph 2, item 1; that is to say, that the creation of a single banovina was discussed. Rather, this was a historic aspiration of the Croatian people, to have the Croatian banovina established once again. And that was the banovina that Mr. Macek had worked on before the Second World War, and this banovina was then established. So the aspiration was to have it renewed in 1991. As for all these other political enactments that were passed in this regard, the general conclusion was that all municipal committees and at the regional community of Travnik, that a struggle had to be waged for a pure Croatian territory which could be annexed. But no one said in which form that was important, but that would be annexed to the Republic of Croatia. That was the basic objective of this document, and we had discussed it for a very long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was this an approach to which you gave any support, yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. This was an approach that was supported by the regional community of the Croatian Democratic Union of Travnik and the municipal committee -- or, rather, the president of the municipal committee of Busovaca or the vice-president of the Croatian Regional Community of Travnik, Mr. Dario Kordic. This is a total deviation from the policy of the Croatian Democratic Union of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina that was led by Mr. Stjepan Kljuic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next exhibit is not in the core bundle; it's 25.1 -- no, I beg your pardon, it is 5755, although in the formulation that you will have, that number doesn't appear. Or it may do, but it doesn't appear in mine. This is dated the 15th of November, from the Croatian-Herzegovinian Travnik regional union, and signed, or with a place for a signature, with the name "Dario Kordic," and in fact, if you look at the original signature there, just visible, it reads --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: What document are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the original, the photocopy of the original. And at the foot of --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's a very poor photocopy. Could you please show this to the Prosecutor and ask him whether this is the document that he's discussing?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, and if you just look where the usher will place his thumb, you will find a signature at the foot of the page.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Put your thumb there, please. Could you have found an even poorer copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If you would look, please, at the body of the text, does it read as follows: The subject is "Reply to the proposed initiative for holding a separate meeting of the Croatian Travnik regional union from the municipalities of Vitez, Travnik, and Novi Travnik." And does it read: "Certain leaders of the municipality and the HDZ from the above mentioned municipalities, after my return from the joint regional meeting of Herzegovina and the Travnik regional union in Grude on 12 November where the unanimous attitude of the Croatian people from all the 26 municipalities dated 13 and 20 June, i.e. all documents signed 15 and 22 October were confirmed, sent a request to me personally to call a session of the Travnik regional union to be held in Travnik. I have, in principle, agreed to this meeting provided that, in addition to Mr. Kljuic and his closest assistants, it also be attended by the most responsible leaders from Zagreb and the Herzegovina municipalities." Mr. Cicak, was there any need, in your judgement, for the attendance of leaders from Zagreb for meetings of the Travnik regional union?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: There would be an answer that has two parts. If the Croatian Democratic Union of Herceg-Bosna is an independent organisation, an independent political organisation in Bosnia-Herzegovina, if that is the way we see things, then there is no need for the representatives of the Croatian Democratic Union of Croatia to come to Bosnia-Herzegovina. Secondly, if we believe that the aspiration of the regional community of Travnik, of the Croatian Democratic Union and the entire regional community of Herzegovina is to be annexed to the HDZ of Croatia, then it was necessary for people to come from Croatia and to present their ideological, political, and other positions at the time. At that time, this was considered necessary for Bosnia-Herzegovina. In this case, this meant a division of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina into two parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Exhibit 39, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Core bundle page 5751, this being a letter, typed letter from Dario Kordic, deputy president of the Croatian Union of Herceg-Bosna, president of the municipal board of the HDZ in Busovaca, addressed to the presidency of HZ Herceg-Bosna, president Mate Boban, deputy president Bozo Rajic, secretary Ignac Kostroman, and to all the leaders of the HZ Herceg-Bosna Croatian Union, the Bosanska Posavina. The subject, resignation of the post of deputy president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. It reads: "I am writing this resignation from the honourable post of Deputy President of the HZ Herceg-Bosna, as the legitimate representative of the Croatian people" -- at some time -- "and 50 minutes on 25 January immediately after the close of the Assembly session. "An honest feeling of belonging to the united Croatian people and several months of personal modest contribution to establishing the internationally recognised Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna in the Croatian Travnik regional union area, and my Croatian being -- with all its heart and soul -- turned towards an independent state of Croatia, do not allow me to act as leader of the Croatian people in the HZ BH whose representatives disgracefully and humiliatingly 'defended' -- sold the historical holy Croatian spirit in those areas. "This attitude will in no way decrease my even greater future involvement as a life-long Croatian activist in the HZ HB working for the welfare of the Croatian people. This act of mine should not be considered as a retreat, but as a moral act of pointing out mistakes which could have been and should have been avoided in order to strengthen the healthy Croatian fighting spirit." Then, following a passage that was not capable of translation, it continues: "... that representatives from HZ HB, with the honourable exception in ... Sarac, tonight showed the miserable face of an amorphous mass of a herd blindly following a less blind leader not having the courage, on behalf of 420.000 Croatians in the HZ HB and 120.000 in Hrvatska Posavina, to state the minimum requirements of the Croatian people. It should have been said this night that the Croatian people will not give in even one millimetre of the 'Banovina' area" -- an illegible passage -- "... which will be clearly defined with the democratic right of Croatians to manage their lives in this area. Not a word (was said) to the Bosnia-Herzegovina TV audience about the sovereign B-H the Croatians wanted. "In my opinion, representatives of the Croatian people from Herceg-Bosna-Posavina, who make up a significant majority among the HDZ representatives in the B-H Parliament, having played a secondary role, behaving like political blind men who allowed themselves to be the executioners of the process of losing the centuries old sovereignty of the Croatian people on the territory of Herceg-Bosna. "By hypocritically and without dignity giving an unreserved support to the SDA in the referendum of B-H citizens for an independent B-H state, these gentlemen, Croatian" -- and then there's a break, and it goes on in capital letters: "INDEPENDENT STATE OF CROATIA FOREVER, AND THUS COMMITTED AN UNFORGIVABLE SIN AGAINST THEIR PEOPLE. "As Deputy President of the HZ HB, I am firmly convinced that the leaders of the HZ HB have not made enough effort to hold an essential meeting of the HZ HB Presidency and of all the representatives from our territory. I believe, that even though I only supported such an approach to this historical hour of the Croatian people in Herceg-Bosna, with a clearly defined opinion which can only be determined among the legitimately elected representatives of the Croatian people in Herceg-Bosna and not in some quasi club of representatives which allegedly represents our people, I carry at least a small dose of historical responsibility to the Croatian people for being part of (the assembly) which did nothing to bring about the only possible, necessary, moral Croatian act and no other. Finally, it should be said that the opinion regarding the historical Croatian area in Croatian unions of Herceg-Bosna and Posavina has not been honestly and openly stated." Postscript: "We have received ..." -- and in quotes -- "... 'generous' promise from Mr. Cengic that the Government will respect the decision of the new regionalisation, primarily on economic bases, so the chances that HZ HB may again become a part of several wonderful B-H regions are 'growing.' "For the HDZ, their good and obedient partner last night the allies appointed the constitutional court judge and reserved the post of president of the B-H National Bank. Mr. Miofil Ljubic became the president of the B-H assembly. So now in the next elections for the president of the B-H assembly we can only wait for the post to be given to the HDZ president Mr. Stjepan Kljuic and then in a 'skilled and wise' manner bring about a Croatian Bosnia and Herzegovina with three leading persons in the state -- president of the state, assembly and government -- and also with several ministerial seats since these seats are not wanted by the Serb people. "Congratulations, with respect," and then the name "Dario Kordic," and a signature. Can you just help us with a few things on this document. He refers to a meeting that had happened, the assembly session, the same day, the 25th of January. Had you been at that meeting yourself, or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was present at that meeting. We discussed this letter several times, and had I not known Mr. Dario Kordic, I would have thought that he was in a special psychological frame of mind. This letter is full of inaccuracies, full of contradictions, so it cannot be taken officially as a serious matter for a socio-political community, so it is quite unimportant. It is of minor significance. It is not worthy of a debate. However, this letter shows something different, and that is that Mr. Kordic firmly adheres to his positions that a Croatian Banovina should be established where the Croatian people would live and that would be annexed -- sorry, I always seem to hit this thing -- and that this would be annexed to the republic of Croatia. Then there is a dozen or so inaccuracies, contradictions, and I don't think that they are worthy of comment. The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was never legitimate or legal. It did not have legitimacy or legality. It was never an expression of the will of the Croat people. It was only the expression of a certain group of people who had rallied together and established the so-called Herceg-Bosna, which was never recognised as an official social organisation, and domestic organisations did not recognise this, and international organisations did not recognise it, of course. International organisations would never stoop that low.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Can I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Cicak, I was going to reflect your observation that the letter may not be worth too much comment. You have answered the specific questions that I wanted to deal with, bar one. Can you just help me with that? It's clear in this letter that he is against certain gentlemen as described, and in his postscript it's clear that he's writing critically of some people. Can you help with the gentlemen who he was against at the meeting? Who were they, if you can remember, and if you can't, say so.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot remember, but it is rather comic, you see. In those days, he was against Mr. Mariofil Ljubic, and he became president of Parliament and therefore his associate. So everything is rather absurd. Mr. Mariofil Ljubic is a descent person who is in the HDZ, and I don't see why he would be against him. As for Mr. Cengic and the others, that is understandable, because they belong to the other party, the SDA, and it is quite normal that there should be differences between them, but animosity towards Stjepan Kljuic, who was the first -- next president of the presidency after Alija Izetbegovic, that was -- it was his turn to take over the presidency, so there was no need to say things against him. There was mention here of Mariofil Ljubic and I don't know who else, but these are all people with whom Mr. Dario Kordic collaborated very closely several months later, so I'm surprised how such an about-turn could have been made, a salto mortale, as they say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just, finally, this: It's said to be a letter of resignation. Did he, in fact, resign at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I forgot to say that. He never really handed in his resignation, nor did he have that in mind. I really don't know why he wrote that and what it served, because nobody even read that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: As for -- in terms of the media and other political organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now, that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether you're coming to this next, but the letter was written to one, two, three, four -- there are five addressees. Was there any reaction from them to the letter?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I wasn't coming to it, but I think that the witness may be able to help us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You've heard Judge Robinson's question, Mr. Cicak. To your knowledge, did any of the people to whom this letter was addressed respond to it in writing, or in any other way?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Respond? You mean in writing?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No one responded in writing, ever. Only in a conclusion, I think it was several months later, we discussed the matter of the resignation of Mr. Dario Kordic and that it would not be accepted, and that even Mate Boban didn't know what it was all about. It was some kind of an ethical act demonstrating his disagreement with the policy, I assume, the policy, combined policy of the SDA, the HDZ, and so on. Nobody responded in writing, and orally this matter was raised only several months later. So it was completely irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But you did say that a decision was taken later not to accept the resignation? I just want to be clear about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean as a particular decision? No, it was part of the conclusions of a meeting, and it was stated in those conclusions that the resignation of Mr. Dario Kordic was not accepted. It wasn't any special separate written decision. That would be too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can I turn, please, to the next exhibit, Exhibit 41. So that the Tribunal can know roughly what the evidence will be, there are a few more decisions that we've got to deal with, and then we will come to the newspaper articles that set the scene for what comes at the very end of this passage of evidence. There are a few more decisions yet to deal with. Not so very many.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could we have a break?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think the witness is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Cicak, would you like a break? We normally have our break at 11.15; that's to give the interpreters a break. Would that be all right with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would be very grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You would like a break now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not a break, a pause. A pause. Not a lunch break. Just a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will have our normal break now. 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Exhibit 41, please, and this is dated the 27th of January, headed, "Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Travnik Subregional Community", and in the list of those attending, six lines down, Mr. Cicak, we see your name listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just to tidy one thing up straightaway, if we turn to paragraph 10 of the conclusions, was it indeed on this meeting, at paragraph 10, that the following was recorded: "Full support is given to the leadership of Herceg-Bosna. The resignation of Mr. Dario Kordic is rejected. However, it is acknowledged as a moral act intended to clear all misunderstandings of political options and further activity of Croatian people in these areas"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before we come back to the body of the document, and simply to deal with something that I want to deal with at some stage, could you please look at the end of the document? And for these purposes, the Tribunal might like, please, to look at the original, as the question I have relates to language and translation. On the original, we see that Mr. Kordic signs underneath a title which is headed "Dop --" you tell me what the title is, and then we'll hear it through the interpreters. What title does he have here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Regarding this document, on the last page it says, "Deputy President of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and president of the Travnik Subregional Community, Dario Kordic," but this is not his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. But at the moment, I'm just concerned with the question of titles, and I'm going to ask you this question, but it may be that, in a sense, I'm really trying to get assistance from the interpreters. Is there a word in your language for "chairman" that is different from the word for "president"? It may be that that indeed can't be interpreted, if there isn't an appropriate word, but --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There is, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What's the word for chairman?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Precidavajuci." "No," says the witness.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Our word for "chairman" is "predsjedavajuci", and "president" is "president." In this case, it is not the chairman of a meeting that is the person chairing a meeting, the first among equals, but this is the president of the Travnik Subregional Community.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And we see here the signature. You say that is not his signature?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Do you know anything about how that signature was put on this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No, I don't. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we come back, please --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I couldn't speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: (Inaudible) of the document, and in the conclusions, I just want to deal with, I think, three of them. Under "1" and about five lines down, does the conclusion read as follows? "Representatives in the Bosnia and Herzegovina assembly, chosen on behalf of the B and H HDZ, should not have voted, nor were they authorised to vote for such a decision, without consulting with the municipal HDZ boards and without consulting with the Herceg-Bosna presidency, as these decisions were decisive for the destiny of the Croatian people." Do you remember this matter being discussed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, at the time the Croatian Democratic Union and its position, ranging from the main board of the HDZ of Croatia to the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina, was that the Croats should not participate in the referendum. At first, that was the position taken, that the Croats should not participate in the referendum.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What was your position on this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: My position was that there was no reason for the Croats to obstruct the referendum in Bosnia-Herzegovina, that they should freely express their will, because, after all, it meant general support but it didn't really mean anything, but it was a kind of moral support for the State of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Conclusion number 6, please. "We state that inter-party negotiations up to now have been consciously obstructed by Stjepan Kljuic, and this subregion withdraws any right bestowed on him for representing the party and the Croatian people." Was that a view with which you agreed or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Nonsense. I did not agree with that. Such a conclusion was not even adopted at this meeting. I said already that all written documents that later appeared, such as these minutes, were drafted by Mr. Kostroman in his own office after the meetings. He would phrase the conclusions in these documents in the way it suited him, his followers and his superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Then paragraph 9, "Mr. Mate Boban shall be in charge of speeding up the negotiations with other parties together with persons authorised to negotiate. Mr. Stjepan Kljuic is to be excluded from negotiations, since his conduct is directly obstructing the course and the content of the negotiations." Do your previous comments apply to that paragraph as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I have no comment. This is a fatal mistake for the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I'm afraid someone from the Defence may again say that I'm commenting on this matter, but this meant complete separation of Mr. Kljuic from the Croatian Democratic Union and the take-over of that union by Mr. Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. Exhibit 42, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have heard several references to decisions taken in these meetings and the question as to whether they have been reflected with fidelity in the conclusions. I would like to find out what was the procedure in the meeting for the adoption of decisions. For example, was it on the basis of a majority, or on what basis were decisions adopted?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Cicak, you've heard Judge Robinson's question. Could you help us, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can. At each meeting, minutes were kept in handwriting, by hand. Those minutes were of a general nature. The debates were also of a general nature. There was nothing specific. And after those discussions, it would be proposed that a group of people attending the meeting, the secretariat or the executive board of the HDZ, would draft the conclusions. Then, on the basis of the minutes and the discussions that went on at the meeting among 20 or 30 men, the main points would be extracted and a sentence compiled in the form of a conclusion. So that in this case, everything that is written here was not adopted by the executive board or a group of people attending the meeting. All these conclusions, at least those at my disposal, and there were several hundred of them, I see only a couple here, those conclusions were drafted by Mr. Ignac Kostroman. I think this suited the interests of a certain group of people in the Croatian Democratic Community.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can I follow that answer with two detailed questions? Were matters at the meeting ever put to a vote of those attending?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How regularly? For every issue or just for some issues?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Some key issues that had to do with the work of the HDZ and the society in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the activities of the HDZ in Busovaca. There are two types of voting; secret ballot and by show of hands. All the voting was done by show of hands; those against, those for. Never did we have any secret vote, even in the case of the most important issues for the work of the Croatian Democratic Union.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: When you found yourself in disagreement with the majority or what you may have thought to be the majority, did you nevertheless cast your vote by show of hands in accordance with your conscience?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't vote, but this would never be shown in any minutes or in any written form, so that we don't know what the situation was at that meeting. I know that there were a number of my friends attending these meetings who did not agree with the debates that we had at the time. There were contradictory views expressed, but never, never, never are opposing views reflected in these documents, only those supported by Mr. Kostroman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: My question may not have been clear, but I think you've explained it. But I'll nevertheless clarify it. Did you vote in accordance with what you believed, when you had a chance to vote by show of hand?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Only if I believed in something. If I didn't believe in anything, I would not raise my hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The second detailed question following on

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON'S ENQUIRY
utterances.text: Minutes of the type we are looking at, were they distributed to those attending the meeting on a regular basis or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's a story for children. Let me explain. No, they were never distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: We usually say "a children's tale" to mean that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I trust that meets the concerns of Judge Robinson and the enquires he wanted to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It does. I mean no doubt others may wish to take this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next exhibit is 42, for which I need only one -- literally one line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, before you go on, paragraph 10 of that last exhibit states, "The resignation of Mr. Kordic is rejected."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, it does. I dealt with that right at the beginning of the evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Z42, Registry page number 5737. Mr. Cicak, this is a --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Excuse me. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This one is dated the 29th of January of 1992. I can't find your name in the list, although it's difficult to find names in these lists. It's excerpts from the minute of the session of the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, expanded to include presidents of the municipal boards of the HDZ BH from the area of Herceg-Bosna, and it was held in Grude. Did you attend this meeting or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The only point I want to take you to is on the fifth English side, so the third English sheet, and in the original it's, I think, at about the same place, about five sheets in, under a paragraph headed, "Re-examination of staff appointments." It is the last sentence of that paragraph which, if you found it, reads, in the English translation, "A candidate who is not a member of the HDZ cannot be appointed to a post in the bodies of the Republic." Were you aware of this decision?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Its effect, so far as the power and authority of the party was concerned, was what?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have to explain that in Bosnia-Herzegovina, with the emergence of national parties, SDS, HDZ, and SDA, absolutely no one, no one, could be elected to the lowest position, to a doorman even, if he was not a member of a national party. Therefore, personnel policy was decided by nationalist parties, be it Bosniaks, Serbs, or Croats, which was fatal for Bosnia-Herzegovina and still is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. The next exhibit, please, 47. This one, I'll just check, was not in the core bundle. I'm grateful to Ms. Somers. The transcript reads "nationalist parties" in the answer to the previous question, and I believe the word was "national," but no doubt it can be corrected, if appropriate. This document, Mr. Cicak, dated the 21st of February of 1992, from the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna to the secretariat to the Zagreb HDZ, the presidency of the HDZ of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the secretariat of the HDZ BH, the president of the Grude HZ-HB, and the municipal boards of the HDZ of the Travnik Regional Community, a document signed under a name, "Dario Kordic." Do you recognise the signature or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And whose signature is it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Dario Kordic's, Mr. Dario Kordic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And the body of this document includes, I think, four paragraphs. I don't want to read all of it, in order to save some time, but the first paragraph -- perhaps I better read as follows: "The historic importance of this moment for the Croatian people of Herceg-Bosna calls for a clear and unequivocal stand by the HDZ BH political leadership with respect to the referendum on the status of Bosnia and Herzegovina. We are absolutely opposed to any disruption of the unity of the Croatian people and the HDZ BH, which took much effort to build and was clearly demonstrated during the main board meeting held in Livno. We therefore believe that the passive and vague stand of the HDZ BH presidency has created fertile ground for the activities of opponents of a unified approach of the Croatian people (for example, the Doboj HDZ and others) and its polarisation. Our opponents are taking advantage of this situation and revelling in our weaknesses." And then after two paragraphs, the fourth paragraph reads: "We give no one the right to depart from the clearly-defined stand of the HDZ BH from Livno for which we voted almost unanimously. We, therefore, see all who disrupt party discipline as destroyers and executioners of the Croatian people as a whole." Mr. Cicak, can you help us, please, with what is being referred to as the conclusions of the meeting almost unanimously agreed to at Livno?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Should I start?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: This document shows the division within the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I don't know if I mentioned this before, but I have to say that the Croatian Democratic Union was actually divided into three regional areas. The basic area was the most active one. In terms of the creation of a banovina and annexation to Croatia, et cetera, that was Herzegovina. The other part was Central Bosnia and the third part was Posavina. It was inhabited by people who were very rich, people who were well off, who had their own family houses, their own land, and it never occurred to them that they should go by some silly book or instructions written by Mr. Anto Valenta about the so-called humane resettlement. They were very close to the Posavina of the State of Croatia. They cooperated with them and they had close ties to them. The other community was Central Bosnia and the third one was Herceg-Bosna. This third document shows that there was a polarisation, and it speaks of the regional community -- I underline "regional community" -- of Herceg-Bosna, and they talk about the Croatian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Those two do not mix because the Croatian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina do not only live in the regional community of Herceg-Bosna but throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is to say, from the Adriatic to the Sava, from the Una to the Drina Rivers. There are Croat people living everywhere. The Croat people said clearly that they disagreed with these positions that were presented here, which was acknowledged in this document as well, that -- this was put pretty roughly, that there are destroyers, et cetera, et cetera -- something very ugly was said about individuals amongst the Croatian people who do not recognise these other representatives of the Croatian people. Mention is made of the referendum here. That is to say, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna believed that the Croats should not vote in the referendum at all. But Croats did vote 100 per cent, and they voted -- that should be remembered, they voted in favour of a unified Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can I just interrupt you briefly, because I --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am interrupted all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I think it would be helpful to the Tribunal to return to the question which you asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I was about to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What was agreed at Livno, in a few words, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You've heard His Honour, Judge May's question. Could you just help us by giving us the answer to that question, please. What was agreed at Livno, in summary?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was agreed upon in Livno that these conclusions of Herceg-Bosna had to be carried out throughout all of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that Croats could not be outside the HDZ. That is to say, if they were in the HDZ, they had to carry out the conclusions of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next exhibit is Z48, and then we'll turn to something different.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is a bad photocopy. Couldn't you find better photocopies?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm afraid, Mr. Cicak, you have the best that we've been able to provide at the moment. If we can find better ones for the Court, you can be sure that we will. But I only need you to turn to the second sheet --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: If this is a good photocopy, if this is a good photocopy, I don't know what a bad one is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If you could be so good as to turn to the second sheet, please, of a document that is dated the 27th of February, and the title of which the Tribunal can see for themselves. I think you'll find that paragraph 3 is sufficiently clear to read, and it reads as follows, in the English translation: "The status of outgoing president Stjepan Kljuic: Up until the authorised organ of the HDZ resolves the issue of the formal-legal and political status of the President of the BH HDZ Stjepan Kljuic, his rights and duties regarding his authority as president of the BH HDZ are suspended and he does not have the right to appear in public on behalf of the HDZ BH." And that is signed at the bottom by typed names of Kostroman and Boban. The meeting is said -- hard to discern -- to have been a meeting of the presidency of the Croatian Democratic Union. Mr. Cicak, did you become aware of this decision?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I knew -- well, an introduction has to be made from the 21st of March, 1991, in order to understand this document, and this signature, I don't know whether it is Mr. Boban's signature, but what was written here made no political sense at the moment in Bosnia-Herzegovina, at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. You've told us on several occasions that you did not agree with the decisions that were being made, and you have also told us that your views were never recorded in the minutes, as we've now seen them, of these meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next exhibit, please, is -- Your Honour, I forgot to give you the core bundle document reference. It's 5721 for that last document, 5721. The next exhibit, 59,1 and -- 59,1 and 59,1A were not in the core bundle. They are documents for which we have summary translations at the moment and I trust full translations after the weekend. They are -- this is the first of a few newspaper articles which I will ask this witness to deal with, one or two in full, the others just by reference to certain passages or to the summaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Cicak, you've heard that we don't yet have full translations into English of all the articles that you've provided us, but -- and this is one for which we have only a summary. What I would like you to do, please, Mr. Cicak, is to look at the original version, to remind yourself in the most general terms of what it says, and then to listen to me as I read the summary of its contents from the English version in order to tell us if, in general terms, the summary reflects what's contained in the original. So if you have the original before you, the summary is that this is an open letter by you, dated the 9th of March, headlined: "The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna is a product of a sick mind." Your open letter read, or was summarised, in this way: "The so-called HZ HB President Dario Kordic and the Travnik region crisis staff launched the initiative to block the roads in the Lasva River Valley and the surrounding area. This idea was then called off and a meeting with the Deputy Prime Minister Muhamed Cengic and General Kukanjac announced. "There are many unknown factors regarding the legitimacy of the HZ HB and its leaders as well as their agenda. This letter attempts to shed light on some of them. "The HZ HB is a product of sick extremists led by Mate Boban -- it was never an expression of the will of the Croatian people in BH. "At a secret meeting in Grude, on 18 November 1991, Boban, Kordic, Santic, Kostroman all appointed themselves as leaders of something they concocted and called it HZ HB. "There was never a decision by the central board of HDZ in BH to create a regional community of Travnik HDZ in BH. "The Travnik regional crisis staff was never officially created. "Mato Boban, Dario Kordic, Vlado Santic and Ignac Kostroman -- all self-appointed wild nationalist officials of the non-existent HZ HB have never been given the authority to act on behalf of the Croatian people in BH. "Not one of the 30 Municipal Assemblies which allegedly made up the non-existent HZ HB has ever made a decision regarding the creation of the HZ HB, nor did it call a referendum of the Croatian people on that subject. "Boban, Kordic and Kostroman have no authorisation to organise roadblocks or act in a way which endangers the lives of innocent citizens of BH. "If Croatia is interested in the welfare of the people in BH they can always offer financial assistance rather than inquire about the production of armament factory in Novi Travnik. "The Croatian, Serbian and Muslim peoples in Kresevo, Fojnica, Kiseljak, Busovaca, Vitez, Novi Travnik, and Travnik have always lived together peacefully. The extremists from any nationalist party are in vain trying to provoke a civil war in the region to fulfil some insane objectives. "Deputy Prime Minister Muhamed Cengic and General Kukanjac should not come for a meeting with the self-appointed insane leaders of the non-existent HZ HB because the only true and legitimate representative of the Croatian people in BH is the Central Board of the HDZ in Sarajevo led by president Stjepan Kljuic. "It is hoped that this letter will help the Croatian people and other citizens of BH find out the truth. Perhaps citizens from other national groups will be encouraged to expose their own non-existent self-proclaimed organisations." First, does the summary I've read out reflect what is contained in the original document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were those views expressed your own genuinely held views?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: This article was divided into three parts. The first part -- I mean, lest there be any misunderstanding, the first part of the text of this written material pertains to the physical obstacles to the withdrawal of armaments, weapons, and other equipment from military factories that were in the Lasva Valley. In the Lasva Valley, the following were operating: Vitez, as the dynamite factory --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Cicak, I'm going to come back to the various resources of the Lasva Valley towards the end of your evidence, and perhaps we can deal with it there. In order to assist the Tribunal to follow the flow of newspaper articles and their conclusion for you, at this moment, if you accept that the views expressed here were your genuinely expressed views, and bearing in mind that we're going to have a full translation of the document before probably your evidence is concluded, we can move on to the next exhibit. So just help us, please. Were these your genuinely held views at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have to mention one fact only, and this Honourable Court has to bear this in mind: This is the final outcome of my powerlessness. No matter how many times I tried, at all levels of organisation of the HDZ of the BH, to point out all the things that were wrong, especially the criminal acts of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and also the criminal acts of the municipal committee of the HDZ of Busovaca, I did not have any support, and I had to address the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina publicly so that I would draw their attention to what was going on in the more extremist part, so to speak, of the HDZ of the BH and to point out the results of that. This article that I wrote is an authentic text that you managed to find somewhere. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Nice, allow me to interrupt you for a few seconds. It seems to me that you haven't told us -- or, rather, you didn't ask the witness to tell us -- which was the magazine or paper in which this document appeared. Which was the magazine? What was its circulation? What was the background of the publication of this letter? Could we have some more information to be able to perceive the possible impact that it may have had?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly. I was going to turn to some of those issues, but not all of those issues, some of which I cannot deal with. If we look at the original 59,1, there is an annotation at the top which probably needs correcting. I'll deal with it through the witness, if the witness can help.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In which newspaper was this article published? Can you help us, Mr. Cicak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: This article was published in the written media of Bosnia-Herzegovina and in the electronic media of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is to say that it was broadcast on Radio Bosnia-Herzegovina or, rather, Radio Sarajevo. It was broadcast on television, the television of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was carried on the Yutel Television, and also in print. In Oslobodjenje, the daily newspaper, also in Nasa Rijec, and the text that I have here is from the newspaper Nasa Rijec, which covered half of Bosnia-Herzegovina; and as much as I could see in certain documents -- I didn't read this -- I found it in some small local papers, this very same text.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm afraid I don't think we're going to be able to assist with circulation figures for the newspapers, but the newspapers concerned were published in -- how widespread were they published within Bosnia-Herzegovina? Locally, or throughout?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We've already dealt with that. Thank you. I was distracted. I withdraw that question, and we move to the next exhibit, 59,2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Nice, we have information about the mass media, the means used to publish this article. Could the witness tell us whether there were any reactions that he was aware of? Was he aware of any reaction following the publication of this article?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'll deal with Your Honour's question in two ways. First of all, there is certainly a reaction coming, but it comes in a sequence of articles, and it's a newspaper article itself, but it's better that we should see that it is in it's right place in the chronology, rather than at an earlier stage. Indeed, the witness has already referred to that article yesterday when he referred to the title "Small Judas." But I will deal immediately with Your Honour's concern in more general terms at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Cicak, was there any immediate reaction to this article, either in press or in any other way? Contacts with you, phone calls, people stopping you in the street, whatever else. Was there any immediate reaction to this earlier article that you published?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is only one of the ten-odd articles I have published. It is absolutely not one article that I published, but some ten or so, but I don't know how many you have in your documentation. I had many more, because they took -- before they took it out of my house. The reaction was a very turbulent one. All the citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina who were democratically oriented phoned me or they saw me in person or at various meetings, and they approved of my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I trust that will meet the immediate concerns. And as we look at exhibit -- if we now look at Exhibit 59,2.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Again, if you have that before you, Mr. Cicak, this is an article published on the 12th of March, a couple of days later, in --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't have this. Would you please be so kind as to provide me with --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The Slobodna Bosna paper?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: 59,2; does the Court have 59,2?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can I see what the witness has got, and perhaps I can help.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
