utterances.text: Again, Mr. Cicak, I'm going to ask you, please, to remind yourself by looking at and scanning the article as I read to the Court a summary of it that we have at 59,2. The summary reads as follows: "The Croatian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina have recently been exposed to a violent appropriation of power and authority by a group of self-appointed so-called leaders of non-existent political creations allegedly representing Croatian communities in BH. This travesty of political process has been further exacerbated by the foolish ruling that the Croats in BH would be represented in Brussels by Mate Boban, Vlado Santic, and Iko Stanic. These three weak-spirited individuals will never able to represent the Croatian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The HDZ leadership consisting of Tudjman, Mesic, and Juric have just made their worst decision ever in sending these three base creatures. Such actions are likely to be extremely harmful for the independence and respect of the HDZ in BH. "Peace-making efforts of Kljuic and some others have been violently opposed by Boban and company because the president Kljuic saw through the insanity of division of BH. The HDZ in BH has unfortunately been rotting from the core with the unprecedented actions of the secretary general of the party Ignac Kostroman who has been plotting to get rid of the party president. This is being done not to improve the standing of the Croatian cause but to continue looting and defrauding of party funds the majority of which -- 72.000.000 DEM -- have arrived from abroad. The corruption involving officials from HDZ leadership is widespread and includes money laundering, buying and selling of armaments, military equipment, oil, coal, foodstuffs, et cetera. "Moreover, his associates in Croatia have participated in creating policies which have resulted in the most senseless war, with 50.000 citizens of Croatia killed and 1.200.000 displaced throughout Europe. Considering that Tudjman has recently stated that Croatia proper has a historic duty to help the Croats in BH, it is important to decline this offer of assistance. The Croats in BH have always known that they had to follow their own counsel without the need for half-baked concepts conceived by sick and deranged persons like Boban, Stanic, Santic, Kordic and Kostroman. "The proud and independent Croatian people in BH will never follow someone like Boban who is not worthy of representing them." First of all, Mr. Cicak -- and I know it's a difficult exercise -- but does the summary that I've read out cover most of the important points in the original text that you've had before you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Partly, it does correspond, but the translation is not quite correct, at least what I heard through the headphones, but the text is okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Again, insofar as it's accurate, were these your honest opinions expressed publicly at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: More loudly, please. Yes. These are my honest opinions, and they were the result of the increasingly deteriorating situation in Herceg-Bosna or, rather, the part led by Mr. Dario Kordic and Mr. Mate Boban. The result of this was the arming of Croats. Whether this was on a voluntary basis or not, I don't know, but an important point of mine was underlined here, and I think it was supported by all the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that is that Mate Boban does not have the legitimacy to represent the Croatian people, especially Vlado Santic and the others. These were anonymous people, and Mr. Mate Boban under no circumstances had the legitimacy to represent the Croats of Bosnia-Herzegovina. If anyone needed to represent them, then there were the official bodies of Bosnia-Herzegovina in which those people were members, and they could have been the people to go to the negotiations in Brussels. Everything else is true, because a large amount of money was obtained through sale of armaments and directly coming to Bosnia-Herzegovina. I think I can freely say that the persons profited personally more than they really prepared the Croatian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina for any kind of military campaign that was being prepared. All this was the result of the erroneous policy of Mr. Tudjman, Mr. Mesic, Mr. Susak, and, of course, there were Spegelj and others working in Croatia, but I think it was a totally erroneous policy towards Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next document, please, is Z60, and is a minute that fits chronologically into the developing history. Registry page number, again, 5709.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This document, I think, is headed as an excerpt from the minutes of a meeting of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina held on the 15th of March of 1992 in Bugojno. Did you attend that meeting or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not attend that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We see that Dario Kordic is listed in the block of guests to the meeting, the fourth line in the English and fifth line in the original. The conclusions of the meeting, at the second sheet of the English and likewise the second sheet of the original, records the following: "Quorum: We note for the record that 38 members of the Main Board are in attendance, which is a simple majority for lawful decision making. "Election of an acting president of the HDZ BiH: Prof. Dr. Milenko Brkic, Minister in the BiH Government, is appointed the acting President of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina with one abstention. "It has been felt that the election of Prof. Dr. Milenko Brkic, a prominent scientist and politically eminent worker, to the position of acting President of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina is a step towards strengthening the Croatian Community. The Croatian Democratic Union has been supporting unity from the beginning. "All members of the HDZ BiH presidency have unanimously agreed to support the new acting President, and recognise him as the lawfully elected leader of the HDZ BiH." Did you become aware of this decision?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean at the time it was taken, on the same day? I did not. But I spoke to Mr. Milenko Brkic several days later. We had a very intimate conversation. We exchanged some jokes. I asked him how come he had been elected, as a well-known linguist, and who, together with Professor Martin Udovicic, how come the two of them were in this group? And this statement that everybody would support -- how did you put it, the Croatian people; I don't remember exactly -- is a mere farce, because it is well known that Mr. Milenko Brkic handed in his unequivocal resignation several days later. He is today in Mostar. He is a university professor and a man of integrity.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: When he handed over the reins, who --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Therefore to this day -- yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: When he handed over the presidency, who took it over? Who was next appointed or elected?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it was Mr. Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we then please turn to the next exhibit, not in the core bundle, 60,1 and 60,1A in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This is another newspaper article which I would like you to look at to remind yourself of it in general terms, to scan it, if you can, as I read the quite short summary. This is an article published in the same newspaper as the first article was published, I think, on the 16th of March. The headline is: "Busovaca is a Town of Hard-working, Wise and Peaceful Citizens." The article is by yourself. The summary of it is as follows: "Busovaca is a town of Croats, Serbs and Muslims who should all live in peace. That is why the policy of people like Kordic is destructive and senseless. Ethnic hatred is provoked artificially and unnecessarily. Absurd staffing policy is being implemented in administration, police, schools, hospitals, and companies. Croatian citizens and youth are being armed in an unprecedented and insane manner. People who are given weapons are often mentally unbalanced, well-known drunks and unstable characters. This has had a profoundly disturbing effect on the peaceful living of the citizens of the Busovaca municipality. Shootings can occur anytime and anywhere. The financial means given to the HDZ are being used arbitrarily and willfully without any control. Without authorisation, the Busovaca municipality has been secretly made part of the non-existent HZ-HB/Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna/ with Mostar as its centre. The Croatian extremists are wrecking the peaceful life of ordinary citizens. No one can fathom why Kordic has decided to destroy peace and downgrade the complete Croatian movement. We ask the nefarious individuals to leave the Busovaca HDZ in BH and let the normal people live in peace." First, was that summary that I've read, in the most general terms, a reflection of the article of which you have the original before you, in Cyrillic text, of course?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this is one of the nice articles written in the local paper, but it was published in all the print media of Bosnia-Herzegovina as well as the electronic media of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This is an article on Busovaca, a town of hard-working wise and peaceful citizens, which Busovaca always was. Busovaca, from the beginnings as a small village, never had any aspirations to engage in any kind of warfare or extremist activities, and even during the Second World War, when fascists were rampant in this area, Busovaca was not a part of it. It only had one Ustasha. So the main point of this is why is Mr. Kordic arming shock groups, a certain number of people and why he's using them to terrorise the population of the regional community or, rather, the town of Busovaca and the municipality, and what was its aim? Why should people be disturbed, and why should cooperation be upset between Serbs, Croats, and Bosniaks, or Muslims, as they were called in those days? That is the point of this article. I think that the population accepted this, because I received a very large number of written comments and oral remarks in agreement, expressing agreement with this text, and a certain number of members of the municipal board of the HDZ, not to mention the republican presidency of the HDZ, supported these positions, and I think that these were normal positions for a democratic state, or a state that had pretentious to become a democratic state.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Exhibit 61 next, registry page 5703.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This document, in the original, is hand-written. It has some signatures at its foot. Do you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I recognise the signature of Mr. Dario Kordic. I don't know whether I was present at that meeting; probably not. I don't know when it has held, because if it was during the night, I couldn't have been present.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, the date at the top, in handwriting, is said to be the 17th of March, which would accordingly follow the articles that we've just been considering, and is said to be a joint meeting of the leaders of the municipal HDZ boards for Since, Busovaca, Vitez, and Travnik, and the listed attendees, ten in number, are set out. Your name is not there amongst them.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I've already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And it was in Vitez. The conclusions of this gathering --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Excuse me, the time is not indicated, the hours. If the meeting was held at 20.00 hours or 19.00 hours, then technically I could not attend. If it had been held earlier on, I could have attended, but I don't know the time when it was actually held.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. The conclusions read: "1. As a municipality bordering on municipalities of the HZ/Croatian Croatian Community/Herbage-Bosna Since is to be included in the defence system of HZ Herceg-Bosna. "2. Ensure the duality of character of the political and defence activities of HDZ branches in the areas of Since which border on Travnik, Vitez, and Busovaca. Such duality of character and co-operation would be carried out through municipal boards, and such character would refer to the following branches," and they're then listed. Paragraph 3: "Command of the Travnik regional community and the Command of the Since municipality should hold a joint meeting and agree on specific implementation of the above. "A meeting with the representatives of HOS/Croatian Defence Force/(HSP)/Croatian Party of Rights, from the district of Travnik and Since should be arranged as part of these meetings. "Mr. Dario Kordic will co-ordinate this activity." Did you know anything of this decision before it was made?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: A moment ago, we were saying that it was necessary to include these gentlemen in the defence system, the gentlemen who were in the HOS, which was also a paramilitary formation that developed from the Croatian Party of Rights. I think Mr. Jadranko and -- what's his name -- I think it was Marko Kraljevic, who was killed later on during the war, were in it. But this is mere parlance, envisaging the inclusion of Since in the defence system of Busovaca, because Since in those days already had a more organised HDZ in military terms, and there was no need for the HDZ of Since to join the municipal organisation of the HDZ of Busovaca, except to make a whole -- both of them together to form a single region. But the point was that the HOS organisation should be placed under the command or control of the HVO; that is, that all the political organisations should be placed under the control of the Croatian Democratic Union.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just to deal with one detail, you referred to the man Kraljevic. What role did he occupy, what job did he have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I think that later, as far as I know, he was engaged with the police. He was very much involved in the police work and its activities in the region. As for HOS, I don't know. But I know that he was killed. I am not sure whether it was in a traffic accident or whether he was assassinated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And Kraljevic, what were his views, if you knew them, so far as integration of the ethnic groups within Bosnia-Herzegovina or separation of the ethnic groups within Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Interpretation) with Mr. Kraljevic, I spoke with Mr. Kraljevic about 10 times or so. Regardless of instructions of the municipal board of the HDZ of Busovaca, I had private conversations with him. It was very hard to establish contact with him, because this man at first used stimulants, which was something quite unacceptable, so that one couldn't have normal conversations with him as to the way in which the defence should be organised. Generally-speaking, in conversation and in communication, he was a very difficult person, in the sense that he would not -- he did not like dialogue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. Exhibit 62, please. While these are being distributed, I'm going to ask the Chamber, at the end of the morning, for a private session, which may take a few minutes but probably not more than five. I don't know how pressed the individual members of the Chamber are to be away promptly at 1.00. I mention it now. We're obviously happy to sit until any hour, but if the Chamber is pressed, it should know that I'm going to want a couple of minutes in private session at the end of the morning. But I only mention it now because we've still got a quarter of an hour to go, and I don't want to cause a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, we'll adjourn the hearing generally at five to 1.00 and hear your application then.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Document 62 is -- I'm sorry about the quality of the photocopy, Mr. Cicak. Again, it's the best that we can manage. It's a military secret document, dated the 21st of March, being a request to the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia but headed "Meeting with the Minister of Defence." It reads as follows: "At the meeting of the commanders of Central Bosnia held on the 17th of March in Busovaca, a meeting with the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Croatia, Mr. Susak, was considered imperative. We would like to request a meeting with you in order to inform you about the current situation in Central Bosnia and the problems we encounter and to receive your instructions." The list of those representatives to attend follows, including Mr. Dario Kordic, set out as being head of the crisis committee for Central Bosnia, vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Did you know anything about the visit of Mr. Susak or the requested visit of Mr. Susak to this area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Interpretation) in relation to this document, we had several discussions in the municipal committee or in a narrower group of the crisis staff or of the HDZ of the municipal committee of Busovaca. However, the point is the following: We could not get the right person from Zagreb who could explain the overall situation to us; that is to say, in the Republic of Zagreb --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Says the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Interpretation)-- and at all the front lines in Slovenia and in other places. So we sought direction information, and never, ever did we manage to get this kind of information. And Mr. Gojko Susak absolutely could not come to Busovaca. He was probably prevented from doing so because of his commitments in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Exhibit 63. For the assistance of the Court, this is the penultimate newspaper article by the witness, and then there will follow the article in reply by the first defendant, and then we'll go on to deal with the facts. Now, it obviously won't be at this session. We'll go on to deal with the facts of what happened to this witness after this exchange of newspaper articles. This one has been, I think, fully translated. I'll probably just deal with it by five to 1.00. Will you please have before you the original -- I'm so sorry -- the original text and follow as I read? This newspaper article, headed, "What Herceg-Bosna, Which Dario Kordic," reads: "On the 5th of March, 1992, on the afternoon news hour, Radio Sarajevo reported the news from a journalist in Novi Travnik that a major blockade of roads from Travnik to Busovaca, Vitez and the mouth of the Lasva Valley would be undertaken on that day. "On that occasion, listeners of Radio Sarajevo were informed that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, that is, its Vice-President Dario Kordic from Busovaca had organised the blockade. It was also said that they abandoned their intention because circumstances had changed and after the crises headquarters for the region made up of the 11 municipalities in the Lasva River Valley, the so-called region of Travnik, had met. "It was also said that the arrival of the Deputy Prime Minister Mohamed Cengic and General Kukanjac was expected to Novi Travnik for talks. "Please print the following, so that citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina can learn the whole truth: "1. The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was never established with the will and the authority of the Croat peoples and a statutory decision of the BH HDZ in Sarajevo, but it was formed of the fruit of the ill spirit of extreme mental incompetents from the HDZ Croatian Democratic Union gathered around Mate Boban. "2. At the secret meeting in Grude on the 18th of November, they elected themselves as leaders of the non-existent Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Mate Boban elected himself president, Dario Kordic and Vlado Santic elected themselves vice-presidents, and Ignac Kostroman elected himself secretary. That could only have been done by a mad political association. "3. Also, the regional community of the BH HDZ Croatian Democratic Union for Bosnia and Herzegovina for Travnik was never established through the will of the Croat peoples and the decision of the BH HDZ of Central Bosnia in Sarajevo. As such, it does not exist. "4. To claim that any crises headquarters was ever founded and established through the will of the Croat peoples and a decision of the BH HDZ Sarajevo central board and decisions of the municipal assemblies in the region is not true. "5. The self-proclaimed, mad, nationalist heads of the non-existent Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Mate Boban, Dario Kordic, Vlado Santic and Ignac Kostroman, have no authority at all from the Croat peoples of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and there is no statutory decision of the BH HDZ central board in Sarajevo that they can represent Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina. "6. Not one of the 30 municipal assemblies that apparently make up the non-existent Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna has ever passed a decision at its session about the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, nor did any of them call for a referendum of the Croat peoples so that they could express their opinion. "7. The Croat peoples did not authorise Mate Boban, Dario Kordic and Ignac Kostroman to organise in their name and erect throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina various roadblocks, organise armed road gangs, hit the unarmed Croat workers and citizens with weapons, and implement the other illegal, mad and deadly activities for the Croat and other peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina. "These ill-spirited people took this right, endangering the lives of the innocent citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina. "8. The self-proclaimed heads of the non-existent Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna are very worried, in the name of the Republic of Croatia, that the army does not get its hands on weapons produced in the factory in Novi Travnik. If the Republic of Croatia and its President Tudjman are so interested in such weapons, why don't they send 150 million Deutschemark for salaries for the workers in the factory. Then weapons would remain in the storerooms, and the workers would not go hungry because they have not been paid. "The Croat, Serb and Muslim peoples living in Herceg-Bosna, in Kresevo, Fojnica, Kiseljak, Busovaca, Vitez, Novi Travnik and Travnik have for centuries co-existed together. Many wars have gone by, many states have changed, but the peoples on this land did not raise arms against each other. "That is why the attempt of mad extremists from any party to disrupt Croats, Serbs and Muslims, start a civil war and realise their mad aims, is useless. If the Bosnia-Herzegovina government, that is, its Deputy Prime Minister Mohamed Cengic and General Kukanjac come for talks with the self-proclaimed mad leaders of the non-existent Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, then the Bosnia-Herzegovina government and Deputy Prime Minister," and they are named, "are placing themselves on the same spiritual level as the others. They cannot allow something like that, can they? They cannot allow themselves something like that, can they? "11. The public, and especially the Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina, have to be told the truth, that there are many self-proclaimed and non-existent political association in Bosnia-Herzegovina, never established through the will of the Croat peoples. "They were created as the fruits of madness and the minds of Croatian nationalistic extremists. With this act the already seriously shaken and almost ruined reputation of the BH HDZ, with its central board in Sarajevo and its legitimate President Stjepan Kljuic, as the real political representatives of the Croat peoples, has been seriously endangered. "Thank you for allowing me this space and time. By publishing these true facts, you will contribute to the Croat people finding out the truth, and with them the other citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Perhaps that will incite the other people so that they too will also tell their people the truth about certain their non-existent and self-proclaimed political associations. "That would be the proper thing to do." And, Mr. Cicak, was that article a faithful representation of your views at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: May it please the Court, since the witness has taken off his headset throughout the entire recitation, and unless he speaks English, he cannot answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's five to 1.00. We'll adjourn now. Mr. Cicak, would you be back, please, on Monday morning at the same time, 9.45, when your examination will continue?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: May I just say this, Your Honour? The gentleman who spoke a few minutes ago, I actually want to say something in connection with what he said. I understood every word that was said. I know that text, and what he said was nonsense. Thank you. I'll be back on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It's possible you'll want the witness, in light of what I'm going to raise in the private session -- I can do it in his presence or his absence, probably preferable in his absence, but he may have to come back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Since he's here --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: To save him the walk, can we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Cicak, would you remain a moment? Yes, we'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: at 1.05 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 26th day of April, 1999, at 9.45 a.m.
